sources.summary: Private White VC’s James Eden says PM should not be criticised for wearing a high-quality British-made brand It has not yet been two weeks since James Eden, the founder of the Manchester men’s clothier Private White VC, saw one of his best-known customers move in to No 10 Downing Street. In any sane world the man who makes the prime minister’s jackets would be popping open the champagne. His garments have been seen by millions of people and described by journalists all over the world writing about Burnham’s buttoned-down style. Continue reading...
sources.title: No apologies, no freebies: the man who makes Andy Burnham’s jackets on how to weather a storm

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The Pulitzer-winning author of Less and Villa Coco explores the art of writing humour – plus 10 of the best novels to make you laugh In March 2020, when the mayor of San Francisco instructed all citizens to remain in their houses due to a pandemic, the first thing I did was order all the books of Agatha Christie. I was not alone; I think many of us immersed ourselves in reliable narratives to drown out the chaos. It did not matter if it ended in marriage or murder; the reliability was what mattered. Later when I realised I would need to hole up for some time, my reading shifted to a different kind of novel. And because, like Christie, our world has an endless supply of new terrors, it is the comic novel that still fills my reading hours. Nobody knows what a comic novel is. And once you start discussing it, all the fun runs out. EB White compared it to dissecting a frog (you’re left with innards and a dead frog) but I would compare it to turning all the lights on at a party: everyone looks terrible and you’ve ruined the party. Most would agree, of course, that Wodehouse wrote comic novels, but I turn to books hardly anybody would classify that way – Moby-Dick by Herman Melville, for instance – that yet seem to me to be a hoot. I think they are books that decide something is funny, as Jerry Seinfeld once defined comedy. In Moby-Dick, it’s a coin nailed to a masthead. In Vladimir Nabokov’s Pale Fire, it’s the worst best poem you’ve ever read. And yet we feel we’re getting at something the most solemn narratives aim for: an understanding of the human condition, of grief, of love, of death. All the big stuff. The comic novels I love are books that could just as easily have been tragedies. It is simply that the author has decided it’s funny. Continue reading...
sources.title: ​What makes a good comic novel? Andrew Sean Greer on the joy of funny writing

thread_text:
御用裁縫談唐寧街風波

曼徹斯特男裝品牌 Private White VC 創辦人詹姆斯·伊登（James Eden），最知名的客戶最近搬進了唐寧街10號——就是英國新任首相安迪·伯納姆（Andy Burnham）。伊登的外套因此被媒體大量報導，但他表示不會因此要求道歉，也不打算免費贈送，只希望首相就當一般顧客對待。

另一邊，普立茲獎得主作家安德魯·西恩·葛里爾（Andrew Sean Greer）談到喜劇小說的難處：好的喜劇小說要讓讀者同時感受到荒謬與人生的沉重，這種平衡並不容易拿捏。

—— 本則來自 The Guardian，2026 年 8 月 2 日發佈，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
threads_text:
御用裁縫談唐寧街風波

曼徹斯特男裝品牌 Private White VC 創辦人詹姆斯·伊登（James Eden），最知名的客戶最近搬進了唐寧街10號——正是英國新任首相安迪·伯納姆（Andy Burnham）。伯納姆一貫的英式風衣穿搭，讓伊登的品牌被媒體大量報導，換作一般品牌大概會開香檳慶祝，但伊登態度低調，他表示不會要求首相道歉或免費贈送商品，只希望對方就當一般顧客對待。

同一天的另一則藝文話題，來自普立茲獎得主作家安德魯·西恩·葛里爾（Andrew Sean Greer）。他談到自己對喜劇小說的偏好：好的喜劇小說要讓讀者同時感受到荒謬與人生的沉重，這種微妙的平衡，是喜劇小說最難寫的地方。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 8 月 2 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: 英國新任首相的外套，出自曼徹斯特一間小廠牌。這間品牌叫 Private White VC，創辦人詹姆斯·伊登，最近意外多了一位大客戶——首相安迪·伯納姆搬進唐寧街10號，穿的正是他家的外套。媒體大量報導這身穿搭，但伊登態度低調，他說不會要求道歉，也不打算免費贈送，首相就當一般顧客對待就好。同一天，還有一則喜劇小說的話題：普立茲獎得主作家安德魯·西恩·葛里爾說，好的喜劇小說要讓讀者同時感受到荒謬和人生的沉重，這種平衡，才是最難寫的地方。
